title: What The Koto Knows (Chas McIvor)
style: jazz lounge piano bar dry wit spoken word observational 98bpm upright bass brushed snare deadpan baritone male vocal koto world instruments Japanese philosophy comedy
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
The koto has thirteen strings
And plays exactly what it needs to
Not more
The Japanese principle of the instrument
Is the same as the Japanese principle of everything else
Precision within stillness

[Verse 2]
You don't strike the koto — you touch it
The difference between striking and touching
Is the difference between making a sound
And asking a sound to happen
The koto asks
The sound arrives

[Chorus]
What the koto knows
Cannot be rushed into
What the koto knows
Has been waiting for you
The string vibrates exactly once for each intention
What the koto knows — is the space between the mention

[Bridge]
Chas heard koto music once in a documentary
About Japan, about ceremony, about patience
He turned to Wilma and said — that's cricket
That is the sound of cricket
The preparation before the movement
The stillness that contains everything that's about to happen

[Verse 3]
The koto and the mbira have never met formally
But they would understand each other immediately
One plays the red dust dawn
One plays the mountain silence
Both play the thing underneath the thing

[Outro]
What the koto knows
What the koto knows
The string is still
What the koto knows
That's my boy
